drafted.title: Improper validation of tool and model input parameters before privileged execution
drafted.description: Agent frameworks, MCP servers, and model-serving backends accept attacker- or model-controlled parameters (file paths, flow/node configs, request fields, tensor shapes, header values) and pass them into execution, deserialization, or file-system operations without validating type, bounds, or format. Because agentic systems route LLM-generated or user-supplied values directly into high-privilege tool calls and inference pipelines with little scrutiny, this generic failure to constrain untrusted input manifests as remote code execution, path traversal, SSRF, privilege escalation, or denial of service across the stack.

drafted.title: XML external entity injection via unrestricted entity resolution in document-parsing tools
drafted.description: An agent tool, MCP server, or library it depends on parses attacker-supplied XML-based content (documents, SAML/SOAP messages, spreadsheet/archive formats, SVGs, config files) with DTD processing and external entity resolution left enabled, so a crafted DOCTYPE/entity causes the parser to read local files or issue outbound requests on the parser's behalf. This gives an attacker arbitrary file disclosure, SSRF into networks the agent can reach, or denial of service via entity expansion, often simply by handing the agent a document to ingest or summarize.

drafted.title: Unsanitized agent or LLM output injected into downstream interpreters
drafted.description: Agent frameworks and MCP/tool-server implementations frequently pass LLM-generated text, tool call arguments, or externally-sourced content (filenames, scraped pages, retrieved documents) directly into a downstream interpreter — a shell, a graph/SQL query engine, a template renderer, a config/manifest generator — without neutralizing special characters. Because the input the interpreter trusts can be steered by prompt injection, poisoned retrieval content, or crafted tool responses rather than only by a human operator, this generic injection flaw becomes remotely triggerable through the agent's normal reasoning/tool-use loop, yielding arbitrary command execution, query manipulation, or privilege escalation on the host or backing services.

drafted.title: Open redirect via unvalidated redirect/callback URL parameter
drafted.description: An agent platform's web, login, logout, or OAuth/SSO endpoint accepts an attacker-controlled redirect, callback, or redirect_uri parameter and forwards the user's browser or authorization flow to it without validating against an allowlist of trusted destinations. Attackers abuse this to phish credentials, steal OAuth/session tokens issued during agent-to-service authorization, or chain into MCP client registration and SSRF-adjacent flows, undermining trust in the agent's identity and delegation handshakes.

drafted.title: Invoke local MCP tools cross-origin via missing Origin/Host validation
drafted.description: An MCP server exposing an HTTP, SSE, or WebSocket transport (often bound to localhost or a LAN interface) fails to validate the Origin or Host header on incoming requests, so a malicious web page rendered in the victim's browser — via a plain cross-origin fetch, a DNS-rebinding trick, or a hostname-prefix bypass of a weak allow-list — can reach the server and invoke privileged tools, read resources, or hijack an in-progress OAuth/token flow as though it were the trusted local client. This breaks the implicit trust model MCP server authors rely on (that only the paired agent/IDE can reach the local endpoint), turning any site a user visits into a remote attack surface against agent tooling and the systems those tools control.

drafted.title: Arbitrary file read/write via relative path traversal in tool/file-handling parameters
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent service accepts a filename, model name, or extension identifier as a tool/endpoint parameter and concatenates it into a filesystem path without normalizing or rejecting '../' / '..\' sequences, letting an attacker escape the intended directory to read, overwrite, or create files elsewhere on disk. Because agent frameworks expose file upload, model/extension install, backup, and settings-apply endpoints directly to tool calls or HTTP clients, this single flaw pattern recurs across many projects and frequently escalates to remote code execution when the written file is later loaded or executed (e.g., extension/plugin install, config overwrite, archive extraction).

drafted.title: Code execution via unsandboxed eval of agent tool/workflow input
drafted.description: Agent frameworks, MCP servers, and low-code agent/workflow builders take attacker- or model-controlled strings — tool-call arguments, LLM-generated tool-call text, workflow expressions, custom node/component code, or YAML/config parameters — and pass them directly into eval()/exec()-style dynamic code evaluators or an escapable code sandbox. Because the evaluator runs with the host process's full privileges, any upstream party who can influence that input (a crafted prompt, a poisoned model response, a malicious workflow or plugin definition) can achieve arbitrary code execution on the agent host, fully compromising confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

drafted.title: Path traversal in agent file upload/workflow endpoints enabling arbitrary file read or write
drafted.description: An agent-adjacent service (MCP server, ML pipeline manager, workflow store, or plugin loader) accepts a filename or path parameter from a tool call, upload, or workflow definition and concatenates it into a filesystem path without normalizing or restricting `../` sequences, letting an attacker escape the intended directory. This lets an unauthenticated or low-privileged caller read secrets/config outside the sandbox or overwrite arbitrary files (including plugins, configs, or startup scripts) to achieve remote code execution.

drafted.title: Unrestricted file-type upload in agent/tool ingestion endpoints leading to RCE
drafted.description: An agent platform's file-handling surface (chat attachment uploader, RAG/document ingestion, vector-store admin, 'send file to AI' tool, etc.) accepts user-supplied files without validating true content type, extension, or storage location, letting an attacker upload a web shell or script disguised as a document, image, or dataset. Once the malicious file lands in a web-accessible or interpreter-reachable path, it is executed by the underlying server or agent runtime, giving the attacker full remote code execution on the host that powers the agent.

drafted.title: Prototype pollution via unsanitized tool/workflow input causing sandbox escape
drafted.description: An attacker crafts tool arguments, workflow/node definitions, or expression payloads containing keys like __proto__ or constructor.prototype that get merged into JavaScript objects without sanitization, polluting Object.prototype for the whole runtime. Because validation routines, VM sandboxes, and expression/templating engines in agent automation platforms (e.g., workflow orchestrators, code-execution nodes) implicitly trust prototype-chain properties, the pollution lets the attacker bypass input checks, escape the execution sandbox, and ultimately achieve arbitrary code execution in the agent's host process.
